target_customer: Discord and Telegram community owners who charge for access to their servers
problem: Community owners had no easy way to charge for and manage paid access to a Discord server; the product began as a way for a friend to sell memberships to his server.
business_model: Payments and membership SaaS, likely a transaction fee or subscription (not stated in sources found)
product_category: Paid community and membership payments for Discord and Telegram

founders.name: Ben Botvinick
founders.background_notes: The YC page gives no background.

technical_complexity.rationale: Stripe payments plus a Discord bot and role assignment are standard integrations that a small team could build quickly.

defensibility.rationale: Multiple rivals sold Discord access and Discord later added native paid subscriptions; switching costs were low.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Discord opened native paid server subscriptions in December 2022, absorbing part of the wedge. The acquirer of Hyper is not named in any source found.

market_need_then: Creators and communities on Discord were looking to monetize in 2020 and 2021; the founder's own origin story is one friend wanting to sell memberships.

branding.domain_note: Held hyper.co, which now redirects to whop.com/sell as of this check.
branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt launch on 2021-09-29; no evidence of fan community or merch.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic word shared by many unrelated Hyper companies, and no press about the brand.

outcome_analysis: Hyper grew from a friend's Discord membership project in 2020 into a YC S21 company with six people and launched publicly on Product Hunt in September 2021. YC lists it as acquired but no buyer, date or price could be found. The domain now redirects to Whop, which suggests the Whop link, but the page does not mention Hyper and no source confirms a deal. A Whop case study describes a customer moving off Hyper. Too little is public to assign factors.
notes: hyper.co redirects (301) to whop.com/sell, but a fetch of that page and a targeted search found no confirmation that Whop acquired Hyper, so acquirer is null. No funding found for this Hyper; seed results in search belong to other companies called Hyper (VTuber avatars, gaming monetization). Competitor results were 2023 to 2025 vendor pages with nothing dated near 2021, so list is empty; Launchpass, Whop and Subscord are later or undated listings.
